subject: MSA & Order Form – IP ownership / training redlines (Stratos Health)
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@stratoshealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com
Cc: stratos-legal@stratoshealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redlines re: IP + training (MSA & Order Form)

Hi Jordan / Neha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams have reviewed the MSA and Order Form and attached a set of redlines focused on IP and product-use limits. High-level asks:

- Stratos needs explicit ownership of customer data and any output/content generated from our inputs (we don’t want downstream claims on derivative output).
- No model training on Stratos data without our prior written opt-in; telemetry and aggregate metrics are OK.
- Any feedback/bug reports we provide should not grant a perpetual unrestricted license for training or commercial exploitation — at minimum a limited license for debugging and service improvement only (and only on an anonymized/aggregated basis).
- Request a contract clause to require deletion of customer-provided data on termination within 30 days unless otherwise agreed.

We’ve attached a tracked-redline MSA and an annotated Order Form. Can you confirm Redwood’s positions and whether legal can accept these or if you’ll propose alternative language? We have a procurement deadline of 2026-02-10 for the initial purchase order, so a ~48–72 hr turnaround would be helpful.

Attachments: [Attachment: Stratos_Redline_MSA_Dec2025.docx] [Attachment: OrderForm_Stratos_v2.pdf]

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Sr. Counsel, Stratos Health
Lina.Gomez@stratoshealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines re: IP + training (MSA & Order Form)

Lina —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Neha (legal) and Vivek (solutions/technical PM) to own the response and give us proposed language. Marissa from CS is cc’d so she can confirm operational feasibility for deletion requests and retention windows.

Initial read / commercial stance from my side:
- We are comfortable confirming customer ownership of customer data and outputs created from that data; we typically grant customers ownership of outputs generated by their inputs.
- We do not do downstream model training on a customer’s raw input data by default. Redwood’s default position is to retain a limited "service improvement" feedback license that allows us to use aggregated, de-identified signals and bug reports to improve the service. We should be explicit that this does not include training a customer-specific model or using identifiable customer content for model retraining without opt-in.
- Deletion on termination within 30 days is reasonable in principle but we need to confirm what counts as backups/retention logs and any regulatory hold obligations. Vivek / Marissa, can you outline the operational steps and exceptions?

Neha — can you produce a redline response (tracked) and a short summary of the legal rationale for the proposed counter-positions? If you can get that back within 48 hours, I’ll push the doc to procurement and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@stratoshealth.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines re: IP + training (MSA & Order Form)

Hi Lina / Jordan —

Thanks for the redlines — I reviewed the tracked changes and have attached a proposed counter-redline (RWI_redline_response_v1.docx) and a short plain‑English summary below. My aim: protect Redwood’s ability to improve the platform while honoring customer ownership and opt-in for training.

Summary of key counter-proposals:
1) Customer data & outputs: We accept explicit language that customer-provided data and outputs generated from customer inputs are owned by the customer. Suggested clause: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Output. Redwood shall have no ownership interest in Customer Data or Customer Output."

2) Training / Model retraining: We will not train on Customer Data without affirmative opt-in. Proposed clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models or create customer-specific model weights without Customer’s prior written consent. Redwood may use aggregated, de‑identified telemetry and usage metrics for general service improvement."

3) Feedback License: We propose a narrow, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license limited to using feedback (bug reports, anonymized usage patterns) to identify and fix defects and to improve service performance and reliability. Importantly, the license expressly prohibits use of identifiable Customer Data for commercial model training and prohibits sublicensing that would expose raw customer data to third parties.

4) Deletion & retention: We can commit to initiating deletion of active Customer Data and Customer Output within 30 days after termination, subject to (i) legal/regulatory holds, and (ii) a short retention period for necessary operational logs (e.g., 90 days for debugging evidence) unless otherwise requested. We will include a schedule of retention categories in the Order Form appendix.

Operational notes (cc: Vivek / Marissa):
- Vivek: confirm whether the 30-day deletion + 90-day limited logs is operationally feasible and what the remediation steps look like so we can put it in the appendix.
- Marissa: confirm any CS dependencies for supporting the deletion process for an enterprise onboarding (playbook, runbooks).

Attachments: [Attachment: RWI_redline_response_v1.docx]

Next steps suggested: Jordan to confirm commercial acceptance; if Stratos agrees in principle, we’ll finalize tracked language and send a DocuSign package for signature.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@stratoshealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com, jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com
Cc: stratos-legal@stratoshealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines re: IP + training (MSA & Order Form)

Neha / Jordan —

Thank you — this is helpful and close to what we had in mind. A couple of follow-ups from our legal: 

- The phrase "aggregated, de‑identified telemetry" is okay, but we’d like a short definitional sentence in the MSA that explains what qualifies as de-identified (e.g., irreversible aggregation and removal of direct identifiers).
- For the feedback license, can you add a 12‑month sunset for uses beyond immediate debugging (i.e., Redwood can use anonymized feedback for improvements for up to 12 months unless we agree otherwise)? Our concern is perpetual open-ended use.
- Deletion: we want a hard 30-day deletion for active data; limited operational logs are acceptable but please cap the log-retention at 180 days.

Procurement note: we have an internal procurement window ending 2026-02-10 — if we have signed docs by 2026-02-05 that would let finance queue the PO.

If you can accept the 12‑month cap on broader feedback use (still allowing debugging/patching beyond that), and the definitional sentence for de‑identified telemetry, I think we can move to signature. Can you update and send the final tracked version today?

Best,
Lina

- Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models without explicit written opt-in.

Lina — I’ll send a final packet (MSA + Order Form + appendix + signature link) as soon as legal returns the updated tracked changes. Appreciate the collaboration — excited to get Stratos onboarded.
